article.title: Microsoft Brings Xbox Backward Compatibility to PC, Launching in Early Release With Four Original Xbox Games
article.summary: Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC launched July 22 with four original Xbox titles, with achievements and more games planned later this year.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Microsoft has launched Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC, letting players run classic original Xbox games on Windows machines and handhelds for the first time, according to an announcement posted to [Xbox Wire](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/2026/07/22/xbox-backward-compatibility-on-pc/) on July 22. The program rolled out in "early release" with four launch titles, and Microsoft says it is the start of a broader push to bring more of its back-catalog to PC over time.

## What We Know

- Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC "launches in early release, starting with four classic original Xbox games, now playable on PC and handhelds for the first time ever," [Xbox Wire](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/2026/07/22/xbox-backward-compatibility-on-pc/) said in the announcement.
- The four launch titles are BLiNX: The Time Sweeper, Conker: Live and Reloaded, Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge, and Fuzion Frenzy, all originally released for the first Xbox console, according to [Xbox Wire](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/2026/07/22/xbox-backward-compatibility-on-pc/) and confirmed by [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2220860/xbox-is-bringing-games-from-its-original-console-to-pc/).
- The games work on PC and on handhelds "including the ROG Xbox Ally and Xbox Ally X," per [Xbox Wire](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/2026/07/22/xbox-backward-compatibility-on-pc/).
- Each game is "now available for purchase on PC and also included with all Xbox Game Pass plans," and existing digital console licenses "now carries over to your PC or handheld," according to [Xbox Wire](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/2026/07/22/xbox-backward-compatibility-on-pc/). [Game Developer](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/microsoft-launches-xbox-backward-compatibility-for-pc) and [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2220860/xbox-is-bringing-games-from-its-original-console-to-pc/) independently confirmed the Game Pass inclusion.
- Through Xbox Play Anywhere and Xbox Cloud Gaming, the same library can now be played "on your Xbox console, cloud, PC and handheld," [Xbox Wire](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/2026/07/22/xbox-backward-compatibility-on-pc/) said.
- The PC versions add graphics options including "up to 4x resolution upscaling, VSync support, Fullscreen and Windowed display modes, anisotropic filtering, enhanced anti-aliasing, and more," plus customizable language and audio settings, per [Xbox Wire](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/2026/07/22/xbox-backward-compatibility-on-pc/). [Game Developer](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/microsoft-launches-xbox-backward-compatibility-for-pc) and [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2220860/xbox-is-bringing-games-from-its-original-console-to-pc/) both corroborated the upscaling and anti-aliasing additions.
- Achievements, a feature the post calls "one of the top fan-requested features," are not available at launch. Xbox says it will bring achievements to "select original Xbox games on both console and PC" later this year, and the four launch titles specifically "will be updated to include Achievements in the coming months," according to [Xbox Wire](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/2026/07/22/xbox-backward-compatibility-on-pc/). [Game Developer](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/microsoft-launches-xbox-backward-compatibility-for-pc) reported the same rollout timing.
- Minimum system requirements listed by [Xbox Wire](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/2026/07/22/xbox-backward-compatibility-on-pc/) call for an Nvidia GTX 950, AMD Radeon RX 550, or Intel Arc A310 GPU; a 4-core, 8-thread CPU such as an Intel Core i3-10300 or AMD Ryzen 3 3100; 8 GB of RAM; 4 GB of video memory; and Windows 11, which [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2220860/xbox-is-bringing-games-from-its-original-console-to-pc/) also noted is required. Recommended specs step up to a Radeon RX 6800S, Nvidia GTX 1070 Ti, or Intel Arc A770 GPU, a 6-core, 12-thread CPU, 16 GB of RAM, and 8 GB of video memory.
- Jason Ronald, VP of Next Generation at Xbox, wrote in the announcement that the effort reflects a desire to keep players' "personal history of epic stories and treasured memories" playable as hardware evolves, a framing [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2220860/xbox-is-bringing-games-from-its-original-console-to-pc/) also quoted. He added that the four-game launch "marks the beginning of a broader effort to preserve Xbox games from the past and bring them to PC over time," a line also reported by [Game Developer](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/microsoft-launches-xbox-backward-compatibility-for-pc).

## What We Don't Know

Microsoft has not said which additional original Xbox games will be added next or on what schedule, beyond the general commitment to keep expanding the catalog. An exact date for the achievements rollout has not been specified beyond "later this year" and "coming months." Regional availability may also vary, since Xbox Wire specifies the games are rolling out "in supported regions."

## Analysis

[Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2220860/xbox-is-bringing-games-from-its-original-console-to-pc/) frames the launch against the backdrop of Sony's move away from physical media, noting the contrast with Sony's decision to end PlayStation disc production. Machine Herald previously reported that Sony has set a January 2028 [end date for disc games](/article/2026-07/04-as-playstation-sets-a-january-2028-end-date-for-disc-games-the-video-game-history-foundation-presses-the-esa-for-a-legal-digital-preservation-path) on PlayStation, a move that drew pressure from the Video Game History Foundation over long-term access to older titles. Xbox's early-release push to keep two-decade-old console exclusives playable on modern PCs and handhelds lands as game preservation remains an active point of comparison between the platform holders.
